channel.title: Verified News
channel.description: Daily news digest — stories confirmed by multiple independent outlets, each with a Community Note and, where available, a verified YouTube news clip. Includes Joke of the day and Quote of the day on the homepage. Wire reprints count as one. Sources exclude BBC, CNN, CBC, and Radio-Canada. Viral on social highlights confirmed true videos circulating worldwide, plus select claim checks.

item.title: Parti Québécois wins minority government — first return since 2014
item.description: The Parti Québécois won a minority government overnight, taking 59 of 127 seats — its first return to power since 2014, but short of a majority. The CAQ was shut out. A sovereignty referendum would come only after 2029. Why it matters: Quebec’s first PQ government since 2014 is a minority (59 of 127 seats), with any sovereignty referendum deferred past January 2029 per PQ campaign statements — a federal–provincial shift for Canada. What changed: Overnight results confirmed a PQ minority and a CAQ shutout; Prime Minister Mark Carney congratulated the winner. Community Note: minority, not majority; ~28% popular vote. Video: Separatists win Quebec election with promise to hold vote on independence (FRANCE 24 English) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gDMpCNteV_Q

item.title: Smith says she has no knowledge of reported separatist–U.S. strategist meetings
item.description: Premier Danielle Smith’s office said Monday she has no knowledge of reported meetings between Alberta separatists and U.S. strategists, and that she opposes separation or Alberta becoming a U.S. state. Sylvestre and Rath denied offering oil, water, or royalties. Why it matters: The premier’s Monday denial and restated opposition to separation or U.S. statehood frame how Alberta’s government is responding to separatist outreach ahead of the Oct. 19 referendum. What changed: On Monday, after a Globe and Mail investigation, Smith’s office denied knowledge of the reported meetings and restated opposition to separation or U.S. statehood.

item.title: Oct. 19 Alberta referendum: special ballots, advance voting, and safeguards
item.description: Albertans vote Oct. 19 on 10 referendum questions, including separation process. Elections Alberta: 652,000+ special ballots approved; packages due by 5 p.m. Oct. 16; advance voting Oct. 13–17. Why it matters: Special-ballot volume and the advance-voting window set the practical timeline for how Albertans can cast ballots on the 10 referendum questions before Oct. 19. What changed: Latest reporting put approved special ballots above 652,000, with packages due by 5 p.m. Oct. 16. Video: Alberta Senate and Referendum Vote - General Information (Elections Alberta) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nDbd2yGHG6o

item.title: Hundreds rally at Churchill Square over Edmonton infill
item.description: Hundreds gathered Sunday at Churchill Square in Edmonton over residential infill. Public hearings are scheduled for Oct. 13. Why it matters: The dispute goes to Edmonton public hearings on Oct. 13 over proposed developments in specific neighbourhoods after Sunday’s Churchill Square rally. Video: Hundreds protest infill in Edmonton (CTV News) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d5GVs9qvVSs

item.title: Six Nations Haldimand Tract trial opens in Toronto
item.description: A civil trial over the Six Nations’ Haldimand Tract land claim opened Monday in Toronto. Compensation ranges cited are claims, not awards; Canada and Ontario dispute liability. Why it matters: Phase 1 of the trial decides Crown liability only on a major Grand River land claim; Six Nations seeks financial compensation, while Canada and Ontario dispute liability.

item.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Moscow region kills two; nearly 900 drones claimed intercepted
item.description: A Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Moscow region killed two people. Russian authorities claimed nearly 900 drones were intercepted. Intercept and casualty figures not independently verified drone-by-drone. Why it matters: Large-scale drone attacks on the Moscow region mark a further escalation in a war that already shapes global energy and security debates, including in Canada.

item.title: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces push toward Bab el-Mandeb; Houthi denial; unverified by AP/Reuters
item.description: Yemeni government and Saudi-backed forces said they drove Houthis from areas around Bab el-Mandeb. Houthis denied the claims. AP and Reuters could not independently verify. Why it matters: Contested claims of shifting control near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait concern one of the world’s busiest shipping choke points.

item.title: Kenya records first Ebola death — imported case from DRC
item.description: Kenya reported its first Ebola-related death after an imported case from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Contact tracing is under way. Why it matters: Kenya’s first reported Ebola-related death is described as an imported case from the DRC, with contact tracing under standard viral haemorrhagic fever protocols rather than confirmed community spread. Video: Kenya reports first-ever Ebola death (FRANCE 24 English) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAMXLpR479Q

item.title: Emera and Canadian Utilities announce $72-billion combination
item.description: Emera, Canadian Utilities, and ATCO announced an agreement to combine into a Canadian utility and energy infrastructure company valued at about $72 billion, subject to approvals. Why it matters: The announced ~$72-billion Emera–Canadian Utilities–ATCO combination would create a major Canadian utility and energy-infrastructure company — with Alberta’s ATCO in the deal — subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

item.title: Canada’s trade surplus widens to $4.2 billion in August
item.description: Statistics Canada reported that Canada’s merchandise trade surplus widened to $4.2 billion in August 2026, partly from exporters front-loading U.S. shipments ahead of new tariffs. Why it matters: August’s wider merchandise surplus, partly from exporters front-loading U.S. shipments before new tariffs, is a fresh official reading on how trade barriers are already shaping Canada–U.S. trade flows.

item.title: [Unconfirmed] Reports of Moscow-region fuel depot fire
item.description: Some reports described a fuel depot fire in the Moscow region. This has not been officially confirmed by independent reporting meeting the digest’s triangulation standard.

item.title: [Viral · Canada · False] Claim: non-Albertans can freely get mail-in referendum ballots
item.description: Viral claim that mail-in voting is open to anyone without residency checks is false. Elections Alberta manually reviews applications and requires Alberta ID with returned packages.

item.title: Science corner: Brain implant decodes speech and gestures together for an avatar
item.description: UCSF ECoG implant with parallel AI decoders lets people with paralysis drive speech and gestures on a virtual avatar at the same time. Peer-reviewed in Nature Neuroscience (Sept. 14, 2026); covered by Nature news, New Scientist, Smithsonian. Early-stage; small participant set.
